title: Keep next from offering work started in a sibling worktree
lead: `next` picks from the index of the checkout it runs in, so an item another worktree has already started still reads as open and is offered as the next slice.
findings_note: S127 docs audit: next_item ignores claims and sibling worktrees

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: With parallel worktrees, each checkout's `.slicer/index.json` records only its own starts. `slicer list` already reads sibling worktrees and marks such items `wt:NAME` (S122), and `start` warns when another branch or worktree name refers to the id (S113), but `ops.next_item` (`src/slicer/ops.py`) consults neither, so an agent following the documented `next --ready` loop in `main` is handed a slice another agent is implementing. The S127 docs pass now tells agents to check `list` first; the tool could do this itself.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ops.py` (`next_item`) and the sibling-worktree lookup `list` uses
- `src/slicer/ai.py` and `docs/agents.md` (drop the "check `list` first" workaround once fixed)
- tests for `next` against a sibling worktree

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. With an item started in a sibling worktree, `next` in another checkout skips it and returns the next eligible item, and `next --ready --json` reports the skip.
2. With no sibling worktrees, `next` behaves exactly as today.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Settle with the project before building, do not infer: whether `next` skips such items by default or only flags them, how the skip appears in JSON, and the cost of reading sibling worktrees on every `next`. Relates to S135's review status, which also changes what `next` offers.

Settled with the owner (2026-09-29):

- Skip an item started or claimed in a sibling worktree and report it; no opt-out flag. An item also started or claimed in this checkout is not skipped (local work takes precedence, as in `list`).
- Report skips as `in_work_elsewhere: [{id, worktree, owner}]`, present only when non-empty like `unspecified`; text adds `skipped ID (in work in wt:NAME)`.
- Apply it to `next` and `status`. The rendered roadmap pointer stays local-only so render remains deterministic; `ops.next_item` takes the sibling map as an argument and stays git-free.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The tests above pass; the suite and `slicer check` pass.
